extracted.intended_audience: patent litigators, PTAB practitioners, and parties to IPR proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis of the PTAB's application of the Fintiv factors when deciding whether to deny institution of an inter partes review, including the role of Sotera-type stipulations and merits considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv factor 1 — stay granted or likelihood of stay
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the court granted a stay or evidence exists that one may be granted if a proceeding is instituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is no request for a stay and no indication a stay is likely, this factor is neutral. Parties should present evidence of a stay request or realistic indications a stay will be granted to shift this factor away from neutral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv factor 2 — proximity of court trial date to Board's deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Proximity of the court’s trial date to the Board’s projected statutory deadline for a final written decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the district court trial is likely to occur months before the PTAB's final decision date, this factor weighs heavily in favor of denying institution. Parties can counter by providing evidence about the assigned judge’s caseload, requested extensions, or other scheduling facts that could alter the trial date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv factor 3 — investment in the parallel proceeding by the court and the parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which the parallel district court proceeding and the parties have invested in the litigation (e.g., stages of discovery, expert reports).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pertinent inquiry concerns investment 'at the time of institution.' Advanced stages (beyond fact discovery, completion of initial expert reports) weigh heavily in favor of denial. Assertions that the litigation is 'still in its early stages' may be rejected if contemporaneous facts show significant investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv factor 4 — overlap between issues raised in the petition and the parallel proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Overlap between issues raised in the IPR petition and those in the parallel district court proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial overlap favors denial, but a petitioner’s stipulation not to pursue the same petitioned invalidity grounds in district court can reduce duplication. However, the PTAB will evaluate whether the stipulation is a full Sotera‑type stipulation (see separate criterion) and will consider whether the IPR challenges different claims than the district court action when assessing overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv factor 5 — whether the petitioner is the same party as the defendant in district court
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the petitioner and the defendant in the parallel proceeding are the same party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the petitioner is the defendant in the district court proceeding and the trial is likely to precede the PTAB's final decision, this factor favors denial of institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv factor 6 — other circumstances, including merits
rubrics_metrics.description: Other circumstances that impact the Board’s exercise of discretion, including the merits of the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petitioner can overcome adverse Fintiv factors by showing compelling merits (e.g., evidence that the claims are plainly unpatentable). The PTAB will assess anticipation/obviousness arguments and whether the patent owner raised substantial issues. Even though institution uses a lower threshold, the Board may treat weak petition evidence as insufficient under factor six to negate other factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full Sotera‑type stipulation (what suffices to avoid discretionary denial)
rubrics_metrics.description: A full Sotera‑type stipulation should extend to any ground 'that could have been reasonably raised' and thus makes discretionary denial inappropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial stipulations that only forebear specific grounds or references (e.g., 'we won't pursue grounds including Nishikawa, Honda, or Iwai') are not full Sotera stipulations. While a partial stipulation can obviate some duplication and may weigh against denial, it will not have the same determinative effect as a full Sotera‑type stipulation that covers any reasonably raiseable ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and evidentiary presentation at institution
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board evaluates the contemporaneous facts and evidence presented at the time of institution (e.g., scheduling orders, discovery status, expert reports, stay requests).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to present evidence about scheduling realities (judge's caseload, extensions sought) or to show a full stipulation can lead the PTAB to give greater weight to factors favoring denial. Presentations should focus on the state of the parallel proceeding at institution and provide concrete evidence where timing or investment is disputed.
